tilted.notes: Torso tilt (mild or pronounced) is acceptable only when elbow extension sufficiently compensates to maintain vertical force direction. Merged from former high_shoulder_tilt (strict) and tilted (mild) — the stricter elbow_angle min of 105 deg is retained as the unified threshold. elbow_rom_deg max guards against excessive arm dip under tilt.

compact.notes: Compact shooters rely on smooth, controlled elbow ROM rather than large leg motion. Max elbow_rom_deg guards against the arm dipping excessively before the pocket.

one_motion.notes: One-motion shots require continuous kinetic chaining from legs to arm with no pause. dip_duration_s max prevents an inadvertent two-motion pattern. knee_elbow_delay_ms min of -150 ms catches early arm release (arm fires well before legs complete). knee_rom_deg min ensures legs contribute meaningfully even in fluid shots.

two_motion.notes: Two-motion shooters intentionally pause between leg drive and arm release; the delay window (0–300 ms) defines that pause. dip_duration_s max of 0.80 s flags an excessively prolonged load phase. elbow_angle_release_deg min catches low release points. elbow_rom_deg max catches excessive arm dip in the set position.

high_apex.notes: High-apex shots require sufficient vertical impulse and full leg ROM. dip_duration_s max prevents the load phase from killing upward momentum. knee_elbow_delay_ms bounds catch both early and late arm release relative to the leg drive. elbow_angle_release_deg min catches the under-extended elbow deviation common in this style.

smooth.notes: Smooth shooters depend on temporal consistency rather than explosive motion. knee_rom_deg min ensures the legs still contribute a baseline extension even in fluid shots — pure arm shooting without leg engagement is a deviation. dip_duration_s max flags disruptions in the smooth rhythm caused by an overly prolonged load.

power_leg_driven.notes: Power-leg shooters generate force primarily from lower-body extension. dip_duration_s max prevents an excessively long load from reducing the effective power transfer window. elbow_rom_deg max catches an arm that dips too deep before the shot pocket — in this style the legs do the work, so the arm should stay compact.

quick_release.notes: Quick releases minimize dip and leg-to-arm delay.

high_release.notes: High release points require greater elbow extension at release. dip_duration_s max prevents a prolonged load from disrupting the upward release timing. knee_elbow_delay_ms bounds catch both early arm release (negative delay too large) and late arm release relative to the leg drive.

rhythm_based.notes: Rhythm shooters rely on consistent temporal pacing. dip_duration_s max is added to catch an overly prolonged load that breaks the rhythm cadence.

deviation_catalog._description: Human-readable index of all detectable deviations. Keys match values in style_constraints deviation_labels. The reasoner maps raw threshold violations to these entries for coaching output.

excessive_dip_time.coaching_cue: Your load phase is too long — shorten the time between the start of your dip and the beginning of your upward drive to maintain momentum into the shot.

late_arm_release.coaching_cue: Your arm is firing too late relative to your leg drive. The legs have already peaked before the arm engages — initiate the arm extension sooner to keep the kinetic chain connected.

early_arm_release.coaching_cue: Your arm is releasing before your legs have completed their drive. Let the leg push lead — hold the elbow back a fraction longer until the legs have transferred their force upward.

low_release_point.coaching_cue: Your release point is too low. Extend the elbow further at the moment of release to push the ball higher and reduce the chance of a blocked shot.

under_extended_elbow.coaching_cue: Your elbow is not reaching full extension at release. Focus on following through completely — the elbow should lock out toward the target, not stop partway.

insufficient_knee_rom.coaching_cue: Your legs are not contributing enough range of motion to the shot. Bend deeper in the load phase and use a full leg extension to drive the ball upward.

excessive_elbow_dip.coaching_cue: Your elbow is traveling through an excessively large arc before the shot pocket. Tighten the set position — keep the ball closer to the release window and reduce the arm's downward travel.

jerky_elbow_motion.coaching_cue: Your elbow motion is inconsistent across the shot. Focus on a fluid, continuous extension rather than a jerky or rushed movement through the release.

jerky_knee_motion.coaching_cue: Your knee bend is uneven or abrupt. Work on a smooth, controlled squat-and-drive rhythm to improve force transfer consistency.

insufficient_drive_for_high_apex.coaching_cue: Your upward drive phase is too short to generate a high-apex trajectory. Lengthen and slow the drive to push the ball on a higher arc.

insufficient_drive_duration.coaching_cue: Your drive phase is too short for your shooting style. Allow more time for leg extension to fully transfer energy into the shot.

insufficient_elbow_arc_for_tilt.coaching_cue: With a tilted torso, your elbow needs to travel through a wider arc to compensate. Increase your elbow range of motion at the shot pocket.

insufficient_arc.coaching_cue: Elbow ROM is below the minimum for your style. Ensure a full, controlled extension through the shot.

insufficient_elbow_arc.coaching_cue: Your elbow arc is too small for a compact shooting style. Even compact shooters need a minimum range of motion to generate clean extension — widen the pocket slightly while keeping the motion tight.

insufficient_dip_for_two_motion.coaching_cue: Your dip is too brief for a two-motion shot. Allow a deliberate pause at the bottom of the load to establish the rhythm separation between legs and arm.

insufficient_dip_for_rhythm.coaching_cue: Your dip phase is too short to establish shot rhythm. Slow down the initial load to build a consistent timing foundation.

preserve_constraints._description: Features or qualities the coaching system must NOT degrade when generating corrections. Sourced from the evaluation dataset. The reasoner surfaces these alongside deviations so coaching cues avoid conflicting advice.

shoulder_alignment.description: The shooter's shoulder angle at release is well-aligned for their style. Do not suggest posture changes that would alter shoulder orientation.

wrist_snap.description: The shooter's wrist snap and follow-through are mechanically sound. Do not give feedback that would disrupt hand position or release finger pressure.

torso_tilt.description: The shooter's torso tilt is intentional and permitted by the tilted style constraint. Corrections to elbow or arm extension must account for tilt rather than trying to eliminate it.

knee_rom.description: When knee ROM is within or above the required range for the shooter's style, do not suggest reducing leg bend. Only flag knee ROM as a problem when it falls below the style minimum.

high_apex.description: The shooter's high-apex arc is a defining stylistic trait. Corrections to timing or leg drive must not flatten the trajectory. Protect drive_duration_s from being shortened.

one_motion_flow.description: The continuity of the one-motion kinetic chain is a core trait. Do not suggest pauses or deliberate separations between leg drive and arm release that would introduce two-motion characteristics.

dip_rhythm.description: The shooter's dip timing is a core rhythmic anchor. When dip_duration_s is within the acceptable range for the style, do not suggest altering its duration. Only intervene when it exceeds the style max.

compact_pocket.description: The shooter's compact set position (low elbow_rom_deg) is intentional. Do not suggest widening the arm arc. Only flag elbow_rom_deg when it exceeds the style max (excessive_elbow_dip).
